v.s: I swear by this city [i.e., Makkah]
v.c: I do swear by this city ˹of Mecca˺—

q: (when you conquer it). (This verse foretold the conquest of Makkah, which occurred in the year after the Hijrah.)
v.s: And you, [O Muhammad], are free of restriction in this city -
v.c: even though you ˹O Prophet˺ are subject to abuse in this city—

v.s: And [by] the father and that which was born [of him],
v.c: and by every parent and ˹their˺ child!

q: We have certainly created man in toil.

(Together with working hard to see to his own needs and those of his family, man also faces many difficulties and calamities during his life. While engaged in this, he has to ensure that he is always follows the injunctions of the Shari'ah and obeys the laws of his land. The list is endless.)
v.s: We have certainly created man into hardship.
v.c: Indeed, We have created humankind in ˹constant˺ struggle.

q: Does man think that none shall ever have power over him
(to take him to task for the wrongs he does)?
v.s: Does he think that never will anyone overcome him?
v.c: Do they think that no one has power over them,

v.s: He says, "I have spent wealth in abundance."
v.c: boasting, “I have wasted enormous wealth!”?

q: Does he think that none sees him?
(Allaah sees all that he does and will punish him for it.)
v.s: Does he think that no one has seen him?
v.c: Do they think that no one sees them?

q: (He does all of this despite the fact that Allaah gave him all the bounties he enjoys. Questioning his ingratitude, Allaah says,)
Have We not given him two eyes...
v.s: Have We not made for him two eyes?
v.c: Have We not given them two eyes,

v.s: And a tongue and two lips?
v.c: a tongue, and two lips;

q: (of right and wrong so that he may choose which path he wishes to follow)?
v.s: And have shown him the two ways?
v.c: and shown them the two ways ˹of right and wrong˺?

q: For what reason does man not emerge from the abyss
(where he is constantly fighting Shaytaan and his Nafs, both of whom are doing their utmost to mislead him)?
v.s: But he has not broken through the difficult pass.
v.c: If only they had attempted the challenging path ˹of goodness instead˺!

v.s: And what can make you know what is [breaking through] the difficult pass?
v.c: And what will make you realize what ˹attempting˺ the challenging path is?

v.s: It is the freeing of a slave
v.c: It is to free a slave,

v.s: Or feeding on a day of severe hunger
v.c: or to give food in times of famine

v.s: An orphan of near relationship
v.c: to an orphaned relative

v.s: Or a needy person in misery
v.c: or to a poor person in distress,

q: becoming of those who have Imaan, those who encourage each other to be patient and those who encourage each other to be compassionate
v.s: And then being among those who believed and advised one another to patience and advised one another to compassion.
v.c: and—above all—to be one of those who have faith and urge each other to perseverance and urge each other to compassion.

q: are the people of the right
(who will receive their records of actions in their right hands on the Day of Qiyaamah).
v.s: Those are the companions of the right.
v.c: These are the people of the right.

q: Those who reject Our Aayaat are certainly the people of the left
(who will receive their records of actions in their left hands on the Day of Qiyaamah).
v.s: But they who disbelieved in Our signs - those are the companions of the left.
v.c: As for those who deny Our signs, they are the people of the left.

v.s: Over them will be fire closed in.
v.c: The Fire will be sealed over them.
